summary.intent: Implement a Ctrl-C (SIGINT) handler for the interactive `callisto add` prompts using the `ctrlc` crate, as approved by a peer session. It should restore the cursor, print 'Cancelled, nothing written.', exit 130, include a pty test, and pass the license audit.
summary.outcome: Added the `ctrlc` dependency and a shared handler in `tty.rs`, installed only around the `add` prompts. Added 3 passing pty tests (Ctrl-C, Esc, and one more), and lint and `just audit` came back clean. Updated the CLI spec and changeset and staged everything with `git add -A`; no commit was made. The `init` follow-up is not done.

repo: `dialoguer` re-exports `console`, so `dialoguer::console::Term::stderr().show_cursor()` works without adding `console` as a dependency.
`ctrlc` is MIT/Apache-2.0, which `deny.toml` allows; `just audit` passes with it.
The pty test uses `rustix`'s pty API (openpt/grantpt/unlockpt/ptsname, tcsetwinsize) to drive input and SIGINT through a real pty.
Lint (clippy) in this repo rejects `let _ =` on results, so the code uses `drop(...)` instead.
Changes to CLI behavior require updates to `docs/specs/cli.json` and a changeset in `.changeset/`.
Test fixtures come from the `callisto-fixtures` crate (`src/git.rs`), and tests live in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/`.

code.finding: Shared Ctrl-C handler. It is installed only while the prompts run, so a Ctrl-C after the write can't print 'nothing written' when a file was written. It ignores Ctrl-C while `$EDITOR` is open, because the editor shares the terminal's process group.
pty tests cover Ctrl-C, Esc and a third case. One initially failed because bare names are not quoted in the written file; the assertion was fixed.

friction: The first pty test run inside the sandbox failed because it needed a real pty, so it was re-run outside the sandbox.
The first pty test run had an assertion failure from wrongly assuming names are quoted in the file.
`let _ =` patterns tripped the lint and had to be rewritten as `drop(...)` with a Python patch.
open_items: Apply the same Ctrl-C handling, theme and prompts to `init`, but only its theme and prompts, since PR #634 (wp-onboarding-friction) already removes the workflow-YAML dump.
Merge origin/main after PR #634 lands to avoid a conflict.
The changes are staged but not committed; a commit message was written to /tmp/claude-501/cmp/commit-msg2.txt and the update to PR #638 is pending.
